description: NLL's in-memory loader table (label names and values, plus other loader-table node types), serialized to file at CLOSE-SEGMENT. Read back by NLL when loading resumes / linking against the segment, and by the symbolic debugger. Not opened at program execution.

verification.status: DECODED 2026-08-17. Writer carved in LINKAGE-LOAD-H02.PSEG (ND-500 code, 210319H02 media): serializer at virtual B001166C called from the CLOSE-SEGMENT worker B00068CC; record copy 'by bmove ...,$0x20' at B0011769, next-pointer rewrite at B0011771, zero end-word at B0011783, size to SMAX at B0006D6D. Layout verified by parsing all 11 real sample files: 10/11 fully conform with 100% ascending values; SL202-FO-L27 (L-era) partially. MON-DEBUG:PROG (nd-500-mon-j04) is NOT a reader - its file-type tables hold only PSEG/DSEG/DATA/PROG.
fileSources: 11 non-empty :LINK files from the 13-floppy corpus in samples/ (1982-1989, twelve products)

structure.fileLengthLaw: always 32*k + 1 bytes for k cells: NLL writes k cells plus a zero end-word, then calls SMAX(32*k); SINTRAN byte count = max byte pointer + 1. The final 0x00 is the first byte of the zero end-word, not a counted terminator.
structure.headerPage: K-era and later: one 2048-byte page at offset 0, all zero except word 0 = 0xFFFFFFFF; records start at offset 2048. 1982/H-era files have no header page. The 2048 quantum is the serializer's page rounding ((cursor+0x7FF) & ~0x7FF).
structure.recordOrder: records are emitted in ascending order of the value word at +8 (selection sort in the serializer - the manual's 'numerically sorted order')
structure.emptyFileLegal: a zero-byte :LINK is legal and common (segment closed with no retained entries, or system-delivered products)

fields.name: link
fields.description: Era-dependent. 1982 (J-era): constant 0xFFFFFFFF. ~1985 (H00): the old in-memory packed elink values. K-era and later: 0x18000000 + byte position of the NEXT record (the record's address in NLL's D-space segment 3; value & 0x7FFFFFF = file position). 8 of 11 samples show exactly 0x18000820 in the record at file offset 0x800.

fields.name: sl
fields.description: Symbol name length. Matches the name at +16 in every conforming record of every sample.

fields.name: nleOper
fields.description: NLE (numeric length) / operator bits; 0 in all sampled label records.

fields.name: ident
fields.description: Language/ident code; 2 in all sampled label records.

fields.name: cw
fields.description: Flag byte, same bit layout as desc-format.json cwBits: bit0 UDEF, bit1 DREF, bit2 DSYM, bit3 CLAB, bit4 DMPF, bit5 GLOB, bit6 SELECT, bit7 OMIT. The serializer's dump filters test bits 0/4/5 of this byte (B001170A-B0011731). Observed 0x10/0x14/0x16.

fields.name: val
fields.description: Symbol value (ND-500 address). The sort key - strictly ascending across records in every conforming sample.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Symbol name, sl bytes; the rest of the 16-byte area is heap slack (this is why bytes past the name looked like shifted fields). Names longer than 16 chars span cells (manual: 20-char truncation).

openQuestions.description: SL202-FO-L27 (L-era NLL) interleaves large length-prefixed string/module regions (auto-load file specifications) with the symbol cells. The node layout of those regions is undecoded - needs the L-series NLL binary.
Tail cells in several samples hold other loader-table node types (trap-handler names like '#FATAL...', code addresses). Their layouts are undecoded.
